memos.risk:
Recommendation: refuse. Do not buy.

Key reasons from the brief:
- Drawdown of 87.9% from the 30-minute high and a 30-minute return of -78.6%. The coin has already collapsed.
- Last 15 minutes: sell SOL 37.4 vs buy SOL 43.2, net flow only +5.8 SOL on a small base, with the price up 26% off a crash. That looks like a dead-cat bounce, not a recovery.
- Bundle share of 48% and a launch bot present, plus a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.94 early on. Heavy early sell pressure.
- Pool depth of 44 SOL means a $20 round trip faces meaningful impact, and a 30-second execution delay on a coin moving this fast can erase any stop.

No size, stop, or hold time I'd recommend fixes this. A $5 ticket with a 20% stop still loses to fees and the likelihood of another leg down. The name and symbol are not a signal either way.

If the desk wants to revisit, the minimum I'd want to see is stabilization: several consecutive intervals with net positive flow, sellers falling well below buyers, and bundle share diluting. Even then, I'd use the smallest ticket ($5), a 25% stop, and a 15-30 minute hold.
memos.scout:
The honest case for buying is weak. The one bullish signal is the last 15 minutes: 121 buyers put in 43.22 SOL against 37.39 SOL sold, a net inflow of 5.82 SOL and a +25.9% return, which suggests a recent bounce with fresh demand. Buyer breadth is decent (406 buyers, top-3 holders at 11.4%).

But the brief undercuts it. The coin is down 78.6% over 30 minutes and sits 87.9% below its 30-minute high, so the recent bounce is a dead-cat rebound from a collapse. In the first two minutes after graduation, sells nearly matched buys (0.94 sell-to-buy ratio), and a launch bot was present. Bundled supply is 48.3%, and the completer holds 66% of the curve, so a single actor can dump on the rebound. The 15-minute net inflow is only 5.8 SOL against a 44 SOL pool, a thin cushion versus 1.4-5.1% round-trip costs. I see no case that real demand will persist 30-60 minutes out. Recommend skipping.
